answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontrivial bond in a public contract before it may post jobs or claim rewards. The contract caps influence by bonded stake, then slashes the bond when independent audits prove fraud, so minting a thousand names does not create free voting power. A vine of linked accounts still has to fund every bond; copper is not enough if the stake is forfeitable, and a mirror identity earns no extra trust without fresh capital. The attacker pays for each fake and risks losing that capital.
